sources.citation: Chaudhary, Mahesh Kumar. 2013 [Glottolog dates it 2014]. Language of Saptariya Tharu. Researcher: A Research Journal of Culture and Society 1(2): 49-62. DOI 10.3126/researcher.v1i2.9885
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology (pp. 50-52) gives 29 consonants + 6 vowels, contrastive aspiration and nasalization, and seven syllable patterns; nothing at all on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Chaudhary, Mahesh Kumar (2014). Language of Saptariya Tharu. Researcher: A Research Journal of Culture and Society 1. pp. 49-62.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for koch1247; this work adds nothing on stress. The article treats 'Saptariya/Kochila Tharu' as one regional variety and its phonology inventory is stated for 'Tharu' in general (it notes the phonology of each regional variety differs slightly), so even its segmental figures are not strictly variety-specific. Full text was read (14 pp.); a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/tone/pitch/suprasegmental returned only the intonation lines.
No stress statement for any Tharu variety; reference lists point to Chaudhary 2014, Eichentopf & Mitchell 2013, Boehm 2003 (Dangaura), Leal 1972 (Chitwan).
